title: Secret Rotation in Conjur
content:
Conjur supports automatic and manual rotation of secrets stored in its vault. Rotation ensures credentials are regularly changed to reduce the window of exposure if a secret is compromised.

## Rotation Methods

### Automatic Rotation

Conjur can automatically rotate secrets on a schedule using rotators. A rotator is a plugin that knows how to change a credential on a target system and update the value in Conjur.

Built-in rotators:
- PostgreSQL password rotator
- MySQL password rotator
- AWS IAM access key rotator
- Azure AD application secret rotator
- LDAP password rotator

### Manual Rotation

Set a new secret value using the Conjur CLI:

```bash
conjur variable set -i db/password -v "new-secure-password-123"
```

Or via the REST API:

```bash
curl -X POST https://conjur.example.com/secrets/myaccount/variable/db%2Fpassword \
  -H "Authorization: Token token=\"<access-token>\"" \
  -d "new-secure-password-123"
```

## Configuring Automatic Rotation

Step 1: Define rotation policy:

```yaml
- !policy
  id: db/postgres-prod
  body:
  - !variable password
  - !variable
    id: rotation/ttl
    value: 30d
  - !variable
    id: rotation/rotator
    value: postgres
```

Step 2: Configure the rotator connection:

```yaml
rotation:
  target:
    host: postgres-prod.example.com
    port: 5432
    database: production
    admin_user: conjur_rotator
  schedule: "0 2 * * 0"  # Weekly at 2 AM Sunday
  ttl: 30d
```

Step 3: Grant the rotator service account permissions:

```yaml
- !grant
  role: !group rotation-operators
  member: !host conjur/rotation-service
```

## Rotation Events and Notifications

Conjur emits events when secrets are rotated:
- rotation.scheduled: Rotation has been scheduled
- rotation.started: Rotation process initiated
- rotation.success: New credential set on target and stored in Conjur
- rotation.failed: Rotation failed (old credential still valid)

Configure webhooks to receive these events:

```bash
conjur webhook create \
  --event rotation.failed \
  --url https://alerts.example.com/conjur-rotation \
  --secret webhook-signing-key
```

## Troubleshooting Rotation

### Rotation fails with connection timeout
Verify network connectivity between the Conjur server and the target system. Check firewall rules and DNS resolution.

### Rotation succeeds but application cannot connect
The application may be caching the old credential. Ensure the application re-reads the secret from Conjur after rotation. Use the Conjur SDK's built-in refresh mechanism.

### Rotation frequency recommendations
- Database passwords: every 30-90 days
- API keys: every 7-30 days
- SSH keys: every 90-180 days
- Cloud access keys: every 30-60 days

## Best Practices

- Always test rotation in a non-production environment first
- Configure alerts for rotation failures
- Use dual-account rotation for zero-downtime credential changes
- Monitor rotation logs for unexpected patterns
- Keep rotator plugins updated to the latest version
